links.outcome: Hallucination rate of LLM answers on textbook-grounded medical QA with passages provided
links.effect: LLaMA-70B-Instruct hallucinated in 19.7% of answers (95% CI 18.6 to 20.7) with passages provided, while 98.8% of responses received maximal plausibility; lower hallucination rates aligned with higher usefulness across models (rho=-0.71, p=0.058).
links.quote: Our findings indicate that, across all scales and architectures tested, current large language models remain unfit for unsupervised clinical deployment, and that human expert oversight is both necessary and the dominant cost driver.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark and clinician evaluation quantifying hallucination rates and clinician preference on medical textbook QA, but does not test an organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
